## Symptom

With `papercusp-substrate-sidecar` flipped ON, the operator logged

```
[substrate-boot] SUBSTRATE_SIDECAR on: spawning sidecar for relocated substrate boot
[substrate-boot] sidecar spawn failed, falling back to in-process: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '.papercusp'
```

and ran the whole hyperbee substrate (corestore + merge + projections + swarm)
**in-process** — exactly the event-loop saturation the relocation exists to remove.
The flag was ON; the feature did nothing. The single-box unit suite was green the
whole time. (Caught only by the P-006 live 2-machine rig verify, on a hand-deployed
current-staging `serve.mjs`.)

## Why the tests missed it

`substrate-boot-wrapper.test.ts` **mocks** `./substrate-sidecar-spawn`, and the
host tests use writable temp dirs. So the one thing that was broken — the *real*
`spawnSubstrateSidecar` running from a packaged, root-owned CWD — was never
exercised. "47 green" covered everything except the failure. The flag's
`DARK_FLAG_CASE: 'incomplete'` tag was, in hindsight, exactly right: the packaged
spawn path was never finished.

## Root cause (two bugs, the first masked the second)

1. **CWD-relative socket.** The spawner, the entrypoint, and the IPC client all
   defaulted the Unix socket to `.papercusp/substrate.sock` — relative to
   `process.cwd()`. In a packaged deploy the operator's CWD is the **root-owned
   install dir** (`/usr/lib/Papercusp/sidecar`), so the `tester` user's
   `mkdir '.papercusp'` is `EACCES`. The spawn threw and `bootSubstrateWithFallback`
   swallowed it into the in-process fallback.

2. **`npx tsx <.ts>` from a bundle.** Even past the mkdir, the spawn ran
   `npx tsx apps/operator/bin/substrate-sidecar.ts`. The packaged operator ships a
   single esbuild bundle, `serve.mjs` — there is no `tsx` and no `.ts` on disk. So
   the relocation could only ever spawn from a **dev tree** (where the bg-host RSS
   win was measured); it was dead in the product.

## Fix

- **`substrate-socket-path.ts`** (new): `resolveSubstrateSocketPath()` — honours
  `PAPERCUSP_SUBSTRATE_IPC_SOCKET`, else an **absolute** `os.tmpdir()` path keyed
  by the main operator pid (two operators on one box never collide). Never
  CWD-relative. The spawner pins the resolved path into `process.env` once so the
  parent IPC client and the spawned child agree.
- **Bundled spawn.** esbuild bundles every module into `serve.mjs`, so
  `import.meta.url` in the spawner *is* `serve.mjs` in a packaged build. The
  spawner now re-execs **that artifact** under `process.execPath` with
  `PAPERCUSP_SUBSTRATE_SIDECAR_MODE=1`; `serve.ts` diverts to
  `runSubstrateSidecarServer()` before any operator boot. Dev (TS source) still
  uses `npx tsx`.
- **`substrate-sidecar-server.ts`** (new): the JSON-RPC server extracted out of
  the bin into operator-core, with **no top-level side effects** — so `serve.ts`
  can import it without an auto-running bin guard firing (in the bundle a bin's
  `import.meta.url === argv[1]` guard would resolve TRUE on every boot and start a
  stray sidecar). `apps/operator/bin/substrate-sidecar.ts` is now a thin dev shim.
- **Pattern reused for spawner-sidecar (WI-344 ③, 2026-06-30).** The identical
  `serve.mjs` re-exec approach was applied to the agent-spawn sidecar
  (`packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/spawner-sidecar-server.ts`, plan
  `spawner-sidecar-offload-2026-06-30`): `serve.ts` now also diverts under
  `PAPERCUSP_SPAWNER_SIDECAR_MODE=1` to `runSpawnerSidecarServer()` before any
  operator boot. The no-top-level-side-effects rule and the absolute socket path are
  both enforced in the new sidecar from the start, closing both P-006 root causes for
  the spawner path before they could recur.

## Verifying it actually engaged

On a host running the fixed `serve.mjs` with the flag ON, the boot log must show
**no** "falling back to in-process", and a real sidecar child must exist:

```
fed.sh <a|b> ssh 'grep -i "spawning sidecar\|falling back\|PAPERCUSP_SUBSTRATE_READY" ~/*.boot.out'
fed.sh <a|b> ssh 'ps -eo pid,ppid,cmd | grep -i SUBSTRATE_SIDECAR_MODE | grep -v grep'
fed.sh <a|b> api GET /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-boot-history
```

## Lesson

A flag being ON is not the feature being on. When a code path only runs in a
**packaged** deploy (different CWD, no dev toolchain, a single bundle), a mocked
unit test proves nothing about it — verify on the real artifact before flipping
the default. Anything that resolves a path/socket/binary relative to `cwd` or
assumes `tsx`/source-on-disk is a packaging bug waiting for production.
